description: INV-6 fail-closed is asserted by the oracle ONLY via a static `have 'exit 1'` grep (test-deploy-akash.sh:25) — there is ZERO behavioral test of any fail-closed path. The behavioral run (lines 44-52) exercises only the HAPPY path (cert exists, dseq parses, bid present, lease ok, manifest ok). None of the six fail-closed branches (missing CLI, unset AKASH_KEY_NAME, no dseq, no bid after poll, lease fail, manifest fail) is driven to assert the script actually exits non-zero AND prints no dseq. Given FIND-001 shows the real dseq parse fails-closed unexpectedly, and HARD 0.24 forbids any fake dseq on failure, the absence of a negative behavioral test is a material oracle gap: a regression that printed a stale/empty dseq on failure would pass this oracle.

evidence.snippet: OUT="$(... bash "$S" testchild ...)"; rc=$? ... ok "$([ $rc -eq 0 ] ...)" ... # only happy path

correctFix: Add negative behavioral cases: a fake that returns no dseq -> assert rc!=0 AND stdout is empty (no fake dseq); a fake whose bid list stays empty -> assert the poll exits non-zero within the window; unset AKASH_KEY_NAME -> assert rc!=0. Assert stdout=="" on every failure path to enforce HARD 0.24.
